en.title: Immortal, Invisible, God Only Wise
en.author: Walter Chalmers Smith
stanzas:
[G]Im[C]mortal, in[Am]vis[D]i[Em]ble, [G]God on[D7]ly [G]wise,
in [C]light in[Am]ac[D]cessi[Em]ble [G]hid from [D7]our [G]eyes,
most blessed, [D]most [G]glorious, the [Em]An[G]cient of [D]Days,
[G]al[C]mighty, [Am]vic[D]torious, [Em]thy [G]great name [D7]we [G]praise.

Unresting, unhasting, and silent as light,
nor wanting, nor wasting, thou rulest in might;
thy justice like mountains high soaring above
thy clouds, which are fountains of goodness and love.

Great Father of glory, pure Father of light,
thine angels adore thee, all veiling their sight;
all praise we would render, O help us to see
'tis only the splendor of light hideth thee.

notes: Text is hymnary.org's representative text (Worship and Rejoice, 2003) -- the near-universal four-stanza hymnal form, matching Trinity Hymnal p.38 line for line. It is not simply a subset of Smith's poem: Smith wrote six stanzas, and stanza 4 here splices his stanza 5 ("Great Father of glory... thine angels adore thee") to his stanza 6 ("All laud we would render; O help us to see, 'tis only the splendour of light hideth Thee"). The Cyber Hymnal prints both Smith's 1867 original and an altered six-stanza singing version; neither is what hymnals print, which is why the hymnary text was used. Lower-case line openings and the straight apostrophe in "'tis" are the source's. Key G confirmed by the hymnchords.net Trinity chart (hymnary's incipit database lists ST. DENIO in A-flat, one semitone away); the chart here follows the published one closely. VERIFIED 2026-08-02: text cross-checked against hymnal.net #14, which agrees throughout (it capitalizes line-initially and prints Smith's "All laud we would render" in stanza 4, the variant noted above). One chart fix: stanza 1's last line had ended on [D7]praise with no resolution -- ST. DENIO's lines 1, 2 and 4 share a melody and cadence on the tonic -- so it now ends "[D7]we [G]praise", matching line 1's "[D7]ly [G]wise" and both consulted charts.
